title: C1571 — Universal heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) #11 connector
introduction:
I use this sheet to keep the named oxygen sensor’s heater, supply and measurement-related connections straight. The housing is the envelope; the cavity and circuit labels tell you which message belongs where. Matching the outline alone does not explain what an individual connection does.

Read the identification table first, locate a cavity in the drawing, then follow its assignment row across to the circuit, wire information and function. Finish with the pigtail table when you need to distinguish a service-assembly reference from a terminal or engineering-shell reference. The shaded position is explicitly marked unused in the assignments.

This is a connector-reading guide. Physical sensor location, connector viewing side, access, test conditions and replacement steps are outside its scope. The gauge convention and metadata-code meanings are unspecified, so the entries must not be turned into wire-selection instructions or dimensions.

edits.why: The drawing has a rounded housing, a rectangular projection at the left, angled tabs at the upper and lower left, and projections on the right. I use those details to navigate the page, then read the cavity labels vertically within each column. The shaded position is at the upper left. These are drawing landmarks, not confirmation of a terminal-side or wire-side physical view. Fpn beneath the illustration provides a housing cross-reference to Hard Shell in the identification table.

edits.text: Read the cavity and circuit assignments
edits.why: Read across a single row to keep the Cavity, Circuit Number, Color, Gauge and Function connected. The function labels distinguish the supply, pre-catalyst heater control, sensor, voltage reference and pumping current. Preserve the first-or-unique wording where it appears, and the first-sensor wording on the other relevant rows; neither wording establishes a physical vehicle location here. The shaded position’s row has no assigned circuit and is marked unused. Terminal Part Number identifies a terminal reference rather than the complete connector assembly. Function names do not supply electrical test limits.

Number ties the pigtail row to Kit List in the summary. Service Part identifies the listed service assembly, while Engineering Shell identifies its housing reference. I keep these separate from the assignment table’s individual terminal references. A pigtail includes wire leads, and its Material, Gauge and Cavities entries describe that assembly; Image names its illustration file. The assembly and circuit gauge entries serve different reference contexts and do not establish a wire-substitution or splicing rule.
